name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+9 district with a well-funded incumbent seeking reelection
Frankel's large financial edge ($1.2M cash vs. $34K) and outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 97-98%
No public polling; challenger Adeimy is minimally funded
model.rationale: Frankel is a well-funded incumbent in a D+9 seat, and her challenger has raised only a fraction of her war chest. Markets price her near-certain, and fundamentals point to a roughly 20-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong GOP national environment could tighten the race, though a flip remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Palm Beach-area district that leans Democratic by about nine points. She has raised over $2.2 million and holds more than $1.2 million on hand, with modest outside support boosting her position.

Republican challenger Deborah Adeimy has raised about $163,000 with limited cash remaining, and no outside groups have engaged on either side. No public general-election polls are available, but prediction markets give Frankel a 97-98% chance of winning. The fundamentals, incumbency, and financial picture all point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
